hero.headline: Run your store on autopilot. Know exactly what you earned.
hero.subheading: SellerHill lists your products, keeps price and stock in sync, buys each order from your supplier and pushes tracking back to eBay. Then it shows the real profit behind every sale — measured, not guessed.

flow.title: Built for one job, done properly

p1.title: One flow, not five tools
p1.description: Listing, repricing, stock, ordering and tracking run as a single pipeline — nothing to stitch together or reconcile by hand.

p2.title: Profit you can act on
p2.description: Confirmed costs and estimates are reported separately. An unknown cost is never quietly rounded down to zero.

p3.title: Rules per product
p3.description: Margin, stock cap and listing template are set item by item — not one blanket rule stretched across your whole catalogue.

features.sectionTitle: The daily work, handled for you
features.sectionSubtitle: The jobs that fill a seller's day — listing, watching prices, buying, chasing tracking — run on their own, around the clock.

asinListing.title: List in minutes
asinListing.description: Add a product and it goes live on eBay with a clean, search-ready title, proper images and the item details buyers filter by already filled in.
asinListing.detail: Search-ready title, gallery images and the item specifics buyers filter by are filled in from your source product — nothing to type twice, nothing published half-finished.

priceStock.title: Price and stock stay current
priceStock.description: When your source price or stock moves, your eBay offer follows in the same cycle. No overselling what you can't get, no leaving margin behind.
priceStock.detail: Every refresh compares your source price and stock to what is live on eBay and only pushes a change when something actually moved, so your listing stays accurate without being touched on a fixed schedule.

autoOrder.title: Orders bought for you
autoOrder.description: An eBay sale becomes a supplier purchase automatically, shipped to your buyer. You set a spending ceiling per account, so it can never overpay.
autoOrder.detail: A matched sale places the purchase on a rotating buyer account and ships straight to your eBay buyer, staying under the spending cap you set — anything at risk of going over it stops for your review instead of going through.

tracking.title: Tracking that files itself
tracking.description: Tracking is picked up as soon as it exists and pushed to eBay, so your order is marked shipped on time — and your buyer sees a clean delivery, not your supply chain.
tracking.detail: As soon as a tracking number exists it is picked up and pushed to eBay as the shipment update, so a sale reads as shipped without you checking in on it.

buyerMessages.title: Buyer messages on schedule
buyerMessages.description: Thank-you, shipped, delivered and feedback requests go out on your own templates, at the right moment, without you remembering to send them.
buyerMessages.detail: Order-received, shipped, delivered and feedback-request messages send themselves on your own wording, at the moment each one is actually true — not a guess at when it probably happened.

multiStore.title: Several stores, one desk
multiStore.description: Run more than one eBay store and more than one buyer account side by side, each filtered and reported on its own.
multiStore.detail: Each store and buyer account keeps its own margin rules, its own reporting and its own automation settings, so running three storefronts never means averaging them into one.

profit.sectionTitle: Most tools show revenue. SellerHill shows what is left.
profit.sectionSubtitle: Every sale is matched to its real cost — what you paid, the tax, the shipping and eBay's cut. When a cost isn't known yet, the number says so instead of pretending.

confirmed.title: Confirmed profit
confirmed.description: Sales whose costs are fully captured. This is the figure you can plan against.

estimated.title: Estimated profit
estimated.description: Costs only partly known. Shown apart, clearly labelled, and never blended into your headline number.

honest.title: Nothing invented
honest.description: A missing cost stays a dash. So when you do see a zero, it is a real zero — not an absence dressed up as one.

pnl.title: Month-by-month P&L
pnl.description: Revenue, costs, margin and ROI across twelve months, on one screen and exportable in a click.

panel.title: This month
panel.footnote: Only confirmed profit counts toward your headline figure.

perProduct.sectionTitle: Your rules. Per product, not per account.
perProduct.sectionSubtitle: One blanket setting quietly costs you money on every product it doesn't suit. Set the margin, the stock cap and the template on the items that need their own.

howItWorks.sectionTitle: Three steps, then it runs itself
howItWorks.sectionSubtitle: Connect once, set your rules once, and the daily work stops being yours.

step1.title: Connect your accounts
step1.description: Link your eBay store and the buyer account you source from. It takes a couple of minutes and nothing is installed.

step2.title: Add products and set rules
step2.description: Bring in the items you want to sell, then choose your margin, stock cap and template — globally, or one product at a time.

step3.title: Let it run
step3.description: Listings publish, prices track, orders get bought, tracking flows back to eBay, and your profit figures keep themselves up to date.

faq.sectionSubtitle: The things worth knowing before you start.

q1.question: How does automatic ordering work?
q1.answer: When a buyer orders on eBay, SellerHill places the matching order on your connected supplier account and ships it to the buyer's address. You set a spending ceiling per account, and any order above it stops for your approval rather than going through.

q2.question: Can I still handle an order myself?
q2.answer: Yes. Automation is a setting, not a lock-in — it can be off entirely, off for a particular store, or stepped over on any individual order you want to place yourself.

q3.question: What happens when something goes wrong?
q3.answer: It stops rather than guessing, and tells you why in plain language. Anything waiting on you — a purchase that couldn't complete, a disconnected store, a listing that fell out of stock — is collected on one page instead of being something you have to go looking for.

q4.question: Why do you separate confirmed and estimated profit?
q4.answer: Because a profit figure you can't trust is worse than none. Until the real cost of a sale is known, that sale is reported as an estimate and kept out of your headline number. When a cost can't be resolved at all, you see a dash — so a zero on your dashboard always means a genuine zero.

q5.question: Do I need to install anything?
q5.answer: No. SellerHill runs in the browser and connects to your accounts directly. There is no extension, no desktop app and nothing to keep running on your own machine.

q6.question: Can I try it before paying?
q6.answer: Yes, two ways. The live demo opens the full application with sample data and needs no sign-up at all. Or create an account and start free — no card is required to begin.

variant1.headline: See it working before you commit.
